bridges.description: Show that the existence of a moral arena favors a morally perfect theistic hypothesis strongly enough to support the motion.
Compare how expected the observed universe and moral agents are under theism and atheism using likelihood ratios.
Connect biological information and function to intelligent agency through claimed cause-and-effect regularities.
Argue that contingent reality ultimately requires an eternal necessary ground and that God is the best candidate.
Show that the presented observations do not distinguish God from non-God alternatives and therefore do not establish the motion.
Use unknown natural causes or a naturalistic-pantheist comparison model to match the explanatory work assigned to God.
Challenge the numerical priors and the restriction of the theistic comparison class used in the Bayesian case.
Argue that involuntary suffering and compelled existence conflict with the morally perfect God under discussion.
Require discriminating, observable predictions before treating an explanation as evidence for God.
